data.long_meaning: Refers to the inner self or inner consciousness. Derived from the words 'antar' (inner) and 'vas' (abode). The name Antarvash carries the meaning “Inner Self” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Antarvash usually hope their child will grow to embody inner self and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Antarvash" symbolizes the importance of introspection, self-awareness, and self-realization in Hindu culture. It suggests that an individual should always look inward to find inner peace and wisdom, rather than seeking external sources for validation or happiness.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Antarvash" holds significant spiritual meaning in Hindu philosophy as it refers to the 'Atman' or the inner self. According to Hindu beliefs, the ultimate goal of life is to realize one's true self and merge with the universal consciousness. The name serves as a constant reminder of this inner journey towards self-realization and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Antarvash signifies the inner guide or the soul within us. It is a reminder that the true wisdom and guidance comes from within and not from external sources. The prefix 'Antar' signifies the inner and 'Vash' means control or guidance. Therefore, Antarvash is the inner guide or controller of our lives.

historical_references.reference: The name Antarvash is mentioned in the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata, which is believed to have been composed between 400 BC and 200 AD. Antarvash is the name of the elephant given to Bhima, one of the Pandava brothers, by the king of Kalinga. This elephant was a valuable gift and helped Bhima in several battles.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to the name Antarvash can be found in the Puranas, a collection of Hindu mythological texts. Antarvash is the name of a sage who was a disciple of the god Vishnu. He is believed to have attained the highest state of enlightenment and achieved a unique form of divine union with Vishnu.

Many individuals use this term to refer to their inner self, or their personal spiritual space.
